History and Physical (H&P – Detailed)

Consult Summary:
32-year-old man with 4-day history of severe headache, subjective fever, generalized myalgias, and a diffuse blanching pruritic rash after recent travel to Thailand; advised to attend an urgent face-to-face assessment today to rule out serious/tropical infection.

History:
• Presenting complaint: Severe, persistent headache for the past 4 days.
• Timeline: Headache began first; subjective fever developed later. Symptoms ongoing without improvement despite OTC analgesia.
• Associated symptoms:
  – Subjective fever (temperature not measured); feels cold but no frank rigors.
  – Generalized muscle aches.
  – Diffuse red, itchy rash over entire body; blanching on glass test.
• Negative review of systems:
  – No photophobia (patient initially said “yes” then clarified “light doesn’t bother me” – conflict noted).
  – No neck stiffness or pain on movement.
  – No nausea, vomiting, or focal neurologic deficits (no pins/needles, no weakness).
  – No cough, coryza, or ear pain.
• Exposures/Risk factors: Returned from Thailand ~1 week ago; multiple mosquito bites; travel companion also unwell.
• Relief measures: Paracetamol and ibuprofen with minimal benefit.
• Exacerbating factors: None reported.

Past Medical History:
• Denies chronic medical conditions.
• No previous surgeries reported.

Medications:
• Paracetamol – dose/route/frequency not documented.
• Ibuprofen – dose/route/frequency not documented.
Allergies:
• Denies drug allergies.

Social History:
• Recent travel to Thailand; mosquito exposure.
• Smoking, alcohol, recreational drugs: not discussed.
• Living situation and occupation: not discussed.

Family History:
• Not discussed.

Physical Examination:
• Not performed in teleconsult; no vitals available.

Investigations:
• None performed to date.

Assessment & Plan:
Issue 1: Acute severe headache with subjective fever post-travel – rule out meningitis, malaria, dengue, and other viral/bacterial infections.
  – Urgent same-day face-to-face GP assessment arranged (clinic hub); if unavailable, attend emergency department.
  – Advise need for full physical exam, neurological assessment, and baseline observations.
  – Likely investigations: CBC, malaria film/rapid test, dengue serology, blood cultures, basic metabolic panel, inflammatory markers as per examining clinician.
  – Continue paracetamol/ibuprofen as needed; maintain hydration.
  – Safety-net: Return immediately for worsening headache, non-blanching rash, neck stiffness, vomiting, confusion, or inability to access urgent review.

Issue 2: Generalized blanching pruritic rash.
  – Evaluate during face-to-face visit to characterize morphology and exclude non-blanching component.
  – Consider symptomatic relief (e.g., antihistamine) if deemed viral/exanthematous.

Issue 3: Recent travel to Thailand with mosquito exposure.
  – Highlight risk of tropical infections (malaria, dengue, chikungunya, Zika).
  – Recommend travel-related blood work as above.
  – Document travel history in GP records for future reference.

General Plan items:
• Provide patient with written/emailed instructions on where and when to attend.
• Advise patient to avoid NSAIDs if dengue suspected until platelet count known.

Quality checks:

Missing expected elements:
• Vitals, physical examination findings, full medication list, smoking/alcohol history, family history.
• Objective temperature measurement.

Internal conflicts:
• Photophobia: Patient initially answered “Yep” to difficulty with light, then immediately clarified light was “fine.” (conflict noted)
• Name discrepancy: Recorded as “John Doe” but clinician later addressed patient as “Ben.” (conflict noted)

Transcript quality:
• Generally clear; minor conversational noise and name inconsistency.
